description:
Migrate protocol-callback dispatch onto the existing dispatch-matrix engine, fixing fz-9i4.7.2 (multi-target protocol direct call unmaterializable on a union receiver).

ROOT CAUSE (verified end-to-end). Protocol callbacks (Enumerable.reduce, ...) are bare FunctionIds with no body (source_publish.rs:185). A call lowers as an ordinary DirectCall; resolve_protocol_call (jobs/semantic.rs:1224) resolves it SEMANTICALLY by intersecting the receiver type with each impl's module_impl_target_ty, emitting one CallTargetSummary per overlapping impl. Concrete receiver -> 1 target -> materializes. Union receiver -> multi-target -> materialize_direct_call_edge (artifact.rs:573) requires single_target() -> fatal 'unresolved multi-target direct callsite'. Confirmed: Enum.take on a list-only program compiles; on list+range it fails (the receiver coarsens to list|range via canonical_activation_key/convergence_collapse because Enum.take does not itself dispatch on the receiver, so it is not in the dispatch mask).

INTENT. The dispatch matrix (src/dispatch_matrix/) is the project's single engine for ordered semantic dispatch -> decision tree. Its doc names protocol dispatch as an intended producer ('protocol dispatch maps outcomes to direct calls or residual fallback') but the producer was never wired -- protocol dispatch is the lone holdout doing construct-specific semantic resolution. The matrix dispatches on type (Region::Type); plan_entry_dispatch already turns typed clause annotations into type_region arms; reachability (reachable_clause_ids/branch_possible) prunes type arms by intersect/subtype so a concrete receiver monomorphizes to one arm.

PROVEN VIABLE. Runtime type dispatch among typed clauses on a union value already compiles and runs in BOTH interp and AOT (check(x::integer)/check(_) called on an integer|atom value selects correctly). So a protocol callback synthesized as a typed multi-clause forwarder (one clause per impl, dispatch on receiver type, body = call the impl) flows through the entire PROVEN pipeline: call to the callback becomes one DirectCall to the dispatcher (always single-target -> fatal error gone by construction); concrete receiver -> reachability prunes to one impl (monomorphic); union receiver -> runtime type-tag dispatch.

SYNTHESIS SEAM. A function's identity is backed by a quoted FunctionSource -> expand -> define_function -> derive_function_surface -> lower -> plan_entry_dispatch. Precedent: build_module_info_function (source_publish.rs:1237) synthesizes a whole function at the quoted-source level. The callback's source can be synthesized from ProtocolDispatch arms (refresh_protocol_dispatch builds arms from protocol_impls_for; each arm carries target ModuleId + resolved impl FunctionId). Arms grow as defimpls are discovered, so the dispatcher is DERIVED from ProtocolDispatch(protocol) and re-derived on change.

OPEN FORK (decide in E.1): source-level synthesis (':: List.t' annotations, max pipeline reuse, but the annotation must resolve to the SAME Ty as module_impl_target_ty -- risk for structs/Range) vs IR-level (build the EntryDispatch with module_impl_target_ty(target) directly as Region::Type + a synthesized minimal LoweredBody of N tail-call clauses -- exact type match, more hand-built IR). Resolve by checking annotation/Ty equivalence first.

SCOPE NOTE: making enum_take_drop_split produce CORRECT output also needs the separate take/drop-returns-empty bug (filed separately). This epic only removes the dispatch compile error.

Re-verify all file:line vs HEAD at execution.
title: [EPIC] Protocol dispatch through the dispatch matrix
